about: The Story Bible scan's precision corpus (TestTheScanProposesExactlyTheCorpusNames). Each case is a book of paragraphs with an empty Story Bible; entries is the exact set of new-entry names the scan proposes, and rejected lists junk the scan once proposed or easily could, which must never appear as a name or an alias. Precision first: a name the evidence does not support is left out rather than guessed.

cases.name: owner examples: I'm, Mr and Because I
paragraphs: “I’m not going back there,” Clara said. “Because I promised Mr Darcy I wouldn’t.”
Mr Darcy frowned. “I’m sorry, but I’ll go alone. I'm decided.”
Because I could not stop, I’m told, Clara kept walking.
“Mr Darcy is waiting,” said Clara, and Mr. Darcy was. I'm sure I saw Mr waiting too.

cases.name: honorifics with and without a full stop, merged variants and possessives
paragraphs: It is a truth universally acknowledged that Mr. Bennet had five daughters, and Mrs. Bennet wished each of them married.
“My dear Mr. Bennet,” said his lady to him one day, “have you heard that Netherfield Park is let at last?”
Mr. Bennet replied that he had not. Mrs. Bennet told him that Mr. Bingley, a young man of large fortune from the north of England, had taken it.
Elizabeth laughed. Jane Bennet only smiled, and Elizabeth said nothing more about Mr. Bingley.
When Mr. Darcy walked into the assembly rooms at Meryton, everyone watched Darcy’s tall figure.
Darcy's pride was the talk of Meryton for a week.

cases.name: first-person narration and contractions
paragraphs: I woke before dawn. I’d been dreaming of the sea again, and I’m sure I heard Tomas calling.
“We can’t stay,” I told him. “You know that. They’ll find us.”
He shrugged. She didn’t. We left at noon, and Tomas carried the lamp.
“Because I said so,” I’ll admit, was not my finest answer. “Yes,” Tomas said. “Okay. Fine.” Don't. Won’t. Can't.

cases.name: shouting and chapter headings
paragraphs: CHAPTER ONE
Chapter 3: The Storm
“GET OUT!” Marguerite screamed. “GET OUT OF MY HOUSE!”
The storm broke over the house that night, and Marguerite did not sleep. STOP, she told herself. STOP.
PART TWO: THE RECKONING

cases.name: names with particles, places, and a first name folded into the full name
paragraphs: Isabel de la Cruz arrived in Santa Fe on the morning train.
Everyone in Santa Fe had heard of Isabel de la Cruz, and of her brother, Diego, who never wrote.
She took rooms on Canyon Road, near the house where Ludwig van der Berg once lived. She waited for Diego.
“Diego is late,” said Isabel.

cases.name: plural and possessive family names
paragraphs: The Hendersons lived next door. Mrs Henderson’s roses were famous.
Every summer the Hendersons hosted a party, and Mrs Henderson invited Arthur.
Arthur’s dog barked at the Hendersons’ gate.
“Sit,” Arthur said.

cases.name: sentence-initial function words and adverbs
paragraphs: However, the rain kept on. Meanwhile the river rose. Suddenly the bank gave way.
Yesterday it had been dry. Tomorrow it would flood again. Still, Ruth waited by the window.
Nothing moved. Everything was grey. Ruth watched the road, and Ruth waited.
Perhaps nobody would come. Although Ruth hoped, nobody did. Then Ruth slept.

cases.name: bare honorifics and forms of address
paragraphs: “Yes, Sir,” the boy said. “Of course, Ma’am. Right away, Sir.”
The Doctor will see you now, said the nurse, and the Captain nodded to the Doctor.
Mr. and Mrs. Okafor arrived late.
Lady Catherine de Bourgh was not pleased. Lady Catherine said so twice.

cases.name: days, months, holidays and interjections
paragraphs: On Monday, Priya wrote to her mother. By Friday, Priya had an answer.
“Oh! Well, Hello there,” said Priya. “Okay, Christmas is in December, God help us.”
In January the snow came; in March it went, and on Monday it came back.

cases.name: two names joined by and stay two names
paragraphs: Tom and Mary went to Paris. Later, Tom and Mary came home from Paris.
Mary was glad to be home from Paris.

cases.name: unicode names, emoji and right-to-left text
paragraphs: 🦎 asked for a beer. The lizard, Zoë, said “שלום” to Zoë’s friend Kofi.
Kofi laughed; Zoë did not. Later Kofi and Zoë left together.

cases.name: a book with no names
paragraphs: I walked. I'm tired. I’ll sleep. Because I can.
We said nothing. They said less. It rained.
OK. Yes. No. Why? Because.
